title: Lives, Livelihoods, and the High Cost of Heat

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍爱的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成一个像是由美丽且有50年历史的艺术品组成的移动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听由爱彼呈现的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This summer, an unrelenting heat wave has taken a devastating toll and has put this year on track to be the hottest ever recorded.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，持续不断的酷暑造成了惨重的损失，并使得今年有望成为有记录以来最热的一年。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Coral Davenport and Dana Smith on what it means to live in this new normal where extreme heat now threatens our way of life and even our very lives.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事科罗拉·达文波特和达纳·史密斯将探讨生活在这种极端高温威胁着我们的生活方式甚至生命的“新常态”意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月10日，星期四。

sentences.en: Coral, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉，欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: I am so happy to be back with you guys.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和大家再次见面。

sentences.en: So, Coral, you cover climate change and climate policy for The Times.
sentences.zh: 那么，科罗拉，你在《时报》负责报道气候变化和气候政策。

sentences.en: And, of course, this summer there's been this intense heat wave going on for weeks and weeks, soaring ER visits, even some deaths.
sentences.zh: 当然，今年夏天连续几周都持续着这种酷暑，急诊就诊人数激增，甚至还出现了一些死亡病例。

sentences.en: You set out to understand something kind of different about the extreme heat, its economic coSt.
sentences.zh: 你着手去了解关于极端高温的一些略有不同的方面，那就是它的经济成本。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这个。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I'm kind of obsessed with being able to put price tags on the cost of climate change to the economy, to people's pocketbooks.
sentences.zh: 好的，是的，我有点痴迷于如何给气候变化对经济和人们钱包造成的成本贴上价格标签。

sentences.en: What is the effect of heat on how much work gets done in the United States, on worker productivity, on how much work is lost, on how much pay is lost?
sentences.zh: 高温对美国完成的工作量、工人生产力、工时损失以及薪资损失有什么影响？

sentences.en: You know, I sort of feel like I'm a climate economic detective.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我感觉自己就像是一个气候经济侦探。

sentences.en: And, Coral, why were you obsessed by this question?
sentences.zh: 科罗拉，你为什么会对这个问题如此着迷？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think that a lot of people, when they hear about climate change, it's just this giant existential threat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我认为很多人在听到气候变化时，只觉得这是一个巨大的生存威胁。

sentences.en: But when it's explained in terms of something that absolutely everyone understands, which is dollars and cents and a specific coSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果用每个人都完全能理解的事物来解释，那就是美元和美分，以及一个具体的成本。

sentences.en: If you are an employer and you understand that extreme heat caused by climate change is actually costing you worker hours or increasing the amount of workers' comp that you have to pay.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个雇主，你明白气候变化引起的极端高温实际上正在剥夺你的工时，或者增加你必须支付的工伤赔偿金。

sentences.en: Or if you are a worker and you understand that it's lowering your payroll or that you just can't do your job as well.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你是一个工人，你明白这降低了你的工资，或者让你无法好好完成工作。

sentences.en: In so many ways, I think this makes it very tangible and specific.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，我认为这让问题变得非常具体和切实。

sentences.en: Anything you can put a price tag on, I think Americans understand more clearly.
sentences.zh: 任何你能标上价格的东西，我认为美国人都能更清楚地理解。

sentences.en: Okay, so you went out to do this economic detective work with the effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你带着气候变化的影响去进行这种经济侦探工作了。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: So, first, Sabrina, I'm going to tell you what I thought I would find.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，萨布丽娜，我要告诉你我原本以为我会发现什么。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Which is something that I think a lot of, you know, readers of the New York Times and listeners to the Daily would expect, which is like, of course, when it's hot,
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是许多《纽约时报》读者和《每日新闻》听众会预料到的，那就是，当然，当天气炎热时，

sentences.en: people work less.
sentences.zh: 人们工作得更少。

sentences.en: But the workers who are affected are outdoor workers.
sentences.zh: 但受影响的工人都是户外工作者。

sentences.en: I mean, that's obvious, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很明显，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Mailmen, construction workers.
sentences.zh: 邮递员，建筑工人。

sentences.en: Farm workers.
sentences.zh: 农场工人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, medical researchers have known for years that when people or workers are exposed to heat, they make more mistakes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，医学研究人员多年来一直都知道，当人们或工人暴露在高温下时，他们会犯更多的错误。

sentences.en: They think less clearly.
sentences.zh: 他们的思维不那么清晰。

sentences.en: They work more slowly.
sentences.zh: 他们工作得更慢。

sentences.en: They have more injuries.
sentences.zh: 他们会受到更多伤害。

sentences.en: So, I really thought this was going to be a story focused on outdoor workers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的以为这将是一个聚焦于户外工作者的故事。

sentences.en: And that was my original pitch, showing like construction workers are working less and they're having more job injuries.
sentences.zh: 这也是我最初的选题，展示建筑工人工作时间减少以及工伤增多。

sentences.en: And what I found is that there's a lot of new economic data showing that heat does hurt outdoor workers.
sentences.zh: 而我发现的是，有大量新的经济数据表明，高温确实伤害了户外工作者。

sentences.en: It's lowering outdoor worker productivity.
sentences.zh: 它降低了户外工人的生产力。

sentences.en: But the bigger effect on the economy in the United States is actually on indoor workers.
sentences.zh: 但对美国经济更大的影响实际上是针对室内工人的。

sentences.en: It is affecting so much more of the indoor economy than we really understood.
sentences.zh: 它对室内经济的影响比我们真正理解的要大得多。

sentences.en: And, Coral, why is that?
sentences.zh: 科罗拉，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: It's kind of surprising, right?
sentences.zh: 这有点令人惊讶，对吧？

sentences.en: You really do think of farm workers and construction workers.
sentences.zh: 你确实会想到农场工人和建筑工人。

sentences.en: In my mind, people inside really wouldn't be affected as much.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，室内的人应该不会受到那么大的影响。

sentences.en: So, why is the bigger impact with indoor workers?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么对室内工人的影响更大呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因有几个。

sentences.en: One simple one is that in the United States, there are far, far, far more indoor workers.
sentences.zh: 其中一个简单的原因是，在美国，室内工人的数量要多得多、多得多、多得多。

sentences.en: So, even if not as many of them are being as affected by heat, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使不是那么多的人受到高温的影响，美国

sentences.en: is not fundamentally an agricultural economy.
sentences.zh: 从根本上来说也不是一个农业经济体。

sentences.en: We are much more an indoor.
sentences.zh: 我们更多是一个室内经济体。

sentences.en: We are an industrial economy.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个工业经济体。

sentences.en: So, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，这说得通。

sentences.en: But the number two is there's so many more indoor workers are exposed to extreme heat, particularly now as we are having more extreme heat than I understood.
sentences.zh: 但第二个原因是，有更多的室内工人暴露在极端高温下，特别是现在我们经历的极端高温比我所了解的还要多。

sentences.en: One big example that was very surprising to me, many, many, many factories in the United States are not air conditioned.
sentences.zh: 一个对我来说非常惊讶的重大例子是，美国许许多多的工厂都没有空调。

sentences.en: And there's a couple of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这有几个原因。

sentences.en: A lot of factories were built 30, 40 years ago at a time when the climate was different.
sentences.zh: 许多工厂是在30、40年前气候不同的时候建造的。

sentences.en: You know, in areas like Ohio or Michigan or, you know, parts of the country where you wouldn't necessarily need air conditioning in a factory.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在俄亥俄州、密歇根州这样的地区，或者你知道的，在那些工厂里不一定需要空调的部分地区。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe workers would have to gut it out for like a week each summer when, you know, you'd have a week of hot temperatures.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，也许工人们每年夏天只需要咬牙坚持大约一周，当时，你知道的，会有一周的高温天气。

sentences.en: But it wouldn't be typical to have days and days or weeks and weeks or, you know, many, many days with temperatures over 85 or 90 degrees.
sentences.zh: 但连续好几天、好几周，或者你知道的，有许多天气温超过85或90华氏度，并不是典型的现象。

sentences.en: Now that that is happening inside of those factories, workers are consistently experiencing days where they are regularly working in conditions over 90 and 100 degrees.
sentences.zh: 现在这种情况正在这些工厂内部发生，工人们经常经历气温超过90度和100度的工作环境。

sentences.en: And I'm talking about Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Kansas, you know, parts of the country where workers are going to work.
sentences.zh: 我说的是密歇根州、俄亥俄州、俄克拉荷马州、堪萨斯州，你知道的，全国各地的工人们去上班。

sentences.en: They're working indoors and they're really, really hot.
sentences.zh: 他们在室内工作，而且真的非常非常热。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Coral, I want to talk about the workplaces and what the actual effect has been on workers.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉，我想谈谈工作场所，以及对工人造成的实际影响是什么。

sentences.en: But before we get to that, can you tell me what the total effect is to the economy, like in actual dollars?
sentences.zh: 但在我们讨论那个之前，你能告诉我对经济的总体影响是什么样的吗，比如用实际的美元来算？

sentences.en: Like what are we looking at here?
sentences.zh: 比如我们在这里看到的是什么情况？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So there's studies on this.
sentences.zh: 对此有相关的研究。

sentences.en: One study shows that right now in the United States, as a direct result of heat, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 一项研究表明，目前在美国，作为高温的直接结果，美国

sentences.en: is losing about two and a half billion hours of work per year.
sentences.zh: 每年大约损失25亿个工作小时。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That translates, as a study found, into about $100 billion of economic loss per year and projects that that would go up to about $500 billion a year by the middle of the century.
sentences.zh: 正如一项研究所发现的，这转化为每年约1000亿美元的经济损失，并预计到本世纪中叶，这一数字将上升至每年约5000亿美元。

sentences.en: So there's, you know, a pretty clear price tag.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，有一个非常明确的价格标签。

sentences.en: And I should say that the economists who work on these numbers, it's new to be putting these price tags.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，研究这些数字的经济学家们，贴上这些价格标签是新出现的做法。

sentences.en: And they say, if anything, these are probably undercounts, underestimates of what this price tag of loss is.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，如果说有什么不同的话，这些可能都是对损失价格标签的低估。

sentences.en: So $100 billion going up to $500 billion in loss, that's pretty dramatic.
sentences.zh: 因此，从1000亿美元上升到5000亿美元的损失，这是相当戏剧性的。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a chunk of change, even in context of federal budgets and, you know, big ticket items like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一大笔钱，即使在联邦预算和诸如此类的大额项目背景下也是如此。

sentences.en: So let's dig into this.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨这一点。

sentences.en: What's causing this economic hit associated with extreme heat?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了与极端高温相关的经济打击？

sentences.en: Like what's that number made up of?
sentences.zh: 比如这个数字是由什么组成的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: To just be sort of really like dollars and cents, employer, corporate about it.
sentences.zh: 如果完全从雇主和企业的角度、从美元和美分来看的话。

sentences.en: Those dollar losses are about specifically the loss of worker productivity.
sentences.zh: 这些美元损失具体是关于工人生产力的损失。

sentences.en: That means that humans don't function well in heat.
sentences.zh: 这意味着人类在高温下无法很好地运作。

sentences.en: When they are hot, they work more slowly, they make more mistakes, they need to take more breaks.
sentences.zh: 当他们感到炎热时，他们工作更慢，犯更多错误，需要更多的休息。

sentences.en: And something that is new now is that researchers have been able to quantify how much less they work when they're exposed to certain amounts of heat.
sentences.zh: 现在的一项新进展是，研究人员已经能够量化他们在暴露于一定量的高温时工作量减少了多少。

sentences.en: So there's a new study that shows when workers are working in 90-degree heat, their productivity drops 25%.
sentences.zh: 因此，一项新的研究表明，当工人在90度的高温下工作时，他们的生产力会下降25%。

sentences.en: And when they are exposed to heat of over 100 degrees, their productivity drops 70%.
sentences.zh: 当他们暴露在超过100度的高温下时，他们的生产力会下降70%。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So you're only really working at like 30% capacity when it's 100 degrees?
sentences.zh: 所以当温度达到100度时，你实际上只能以30%的产能工作？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of amazing that they're actually able to put a price tag on it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们居然能够给它贴上价格标签，这真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: But what are some examples of what we mean when we talk about productivity going down, like from the lives of workers?
sentences.zh: 但是，当我们谈论生产力下降时，比如从工人的生活中来看，有哪些具体的例子？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So I talked to a lot of workers for this story, people who work in different kinds of indoor and outdoor environments.
sentences.zh: 所以为了这个故事，我采访了很多工人，他们在各种不同的室内和室外环境中工作。

sentences.en: And it's pretty simple, you know, the workers who are getting hot, they're getting exhausted or sick.
sentences.zh: 这很简单，你知道，变热的工人们，他们精疲力竭或生病了。

sentences.en: So they need more breaks, they need more time off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要更多的休息，需要更多的时间休假。

sentences.en: In some cases, when the heat is too much, the work just doesn't get done at all, it gets postponed.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，当热度过高时，工作根本无法完成，只能延期。

sentences.en: When they get dizzy or can't think clearly, there are more accidents, there are more mistakes.
sentences.zh: 当他们头晕或无法清晰思考时，就会有更多的事故，更多的错误。

sentences.en: And so there's less work getting done, less hours being completed, more breaks, more time off, and more mistakes.
sentences.zh: 因此，完成的工作减少了，完成的小时数减少了，休息更多了，请假更多了，错误也更多了。

sentences.en: And I talked to factory managers, I talked to people who work in warehouses who say, in some cases, we just need to let people leave work early.
sentences.zh: 我采访了工厂经理，采访了在仓库工作的人，他们说，在某些情况下，我们只需要让员工提早下班。

sentences.en: Or, you know, we can tell if people have heat exhaustion that they should not come back to work for a day or two.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，如果发现员工有中暑衰竭的迹象，我们可以告诉他们一两天内不要来上班。

sentences.en: All of that is what responsible employers should be doing.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是负责任的雇主应该做的事情。

sentences.en: It also means that less work gets done.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着完成的工作变少了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like we're not meant to work in that kind of heat, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我们不是为了在那样的酷热中工作而生的一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And the thing is, too, I mean, the effects go beyond productivity, go beyond lost working hours.
sentences.zh: 而且问题还在于，我的意思是，这些影响超出了生产力，超出了损失的工作时间。

sentences.en: I talked to workers in a meatpacking plant in Kansas who talked about how this is a part of the country that's experiencing so much more heat than usual.
sentences.zh: 我采访了堪萨斯州一家肉类加工厂的工人，他们谈到这个地区的温度比平时高得多。

sentences.en: The workers inside this plant are getting exposed to so much more heat.
sentences.zh: 这家工厂内部的工人正暴露在更多的高温下。

sentences.en: And they describe goggles fogging up, not being able to see clearly.
sentences.zh: 他们描述了护目镜起雾、无法看清的情况。

sentences.en: And when that consistently happens, a lot of these workers said, you know, there's a huge risk for food contamination, for meat contamination.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况不断发生时，许多工人说，你知道的，食品污染、肉类污染存在巨大风险。

sentences.en: When we're so hot and we can't even see to do our jobs, you know, one of the workers specifically described, we're working with carcasses and manure,
sentences.zh: 当我们如此炎热以至于甚至无法看清来完成工作时，你知道的，其中一个工人具体描述道，我们正在处理胴体和粪便，

sentences.en: flex of manure could get in the meat.
sentences.zh: 粪便微粒可能会进到肉里。

sentences.en: If you can't see what you're doing and you're so hot, you can't think straight.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到自己在做什么而且热得脑子不清醒。

sentences.en: Something else I heard from a lot of factories, a lot of plants is much higher turnover,
sentences.zh: 我从很多工厂、许多车间听到的另一件事是更高的员工流失率，

sentences.en: much higher percentages of people leaving and fewer people wanting to take the jobs where they would be exposed to heat.
sentences.zh: 更高比例的人离职，以及更少的人愿意接受会让他们暴露在高温下的工作。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So given the cost in terms of productivity, which I assume, you know, companies understand and are kind of trying to think about, not to mention, of course, basic human decency,
sentences.zh: 因此，考虑到生产力方面的成本，我猜，你知道的，公司对此有所理解并正在努力思考，更不用说基本的道德底线了，

sentences.en: having AC when it's 100 degrees.
sentences.zh: 在气温达到100度时有空调。

sentences.en: Why have employers been allowing their facilities to get so hot?
sentences.zh: 为什么雇主一直允许他们的设施变得如此炎热？

sentences.en: So again,
sentences.zh: 所以同样，

sentences.en: one of the sort of big eye opening moments for me in reporting the story was specifically discovering how many factories and sort of indoor industrial facilities in the United States are not air conditioned.
sentences.zh: 我在报道这个故事时的一个重大开眼时刻，就是具体发现美国有多少工厂和室内工业设施没有空调。

sentences.en: Again, in part because many of them are decades old, built in places and at times where we did not consistently experience so much extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 同样，部分原因是其中许多已有数十年历史，建在过去我们不会持续经历如此多极端高温的地方和时期。

sentences.en: So it wasn't necessary.
sentences.zh: 所以当时没有这个必要。

sentences.en: And then now it is wildly expensive to install cooling units in gigantic industrial facilities.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在庞大的工业设施中安装冷却装置的费用极其昂贵。

sentences.en: I'm talking hundreds of millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我说的是数亿美元。

sentences.en: And so for this story, we did talk to a school bus manufacturing plant in Tulsa.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了这个故事，我们确实采访了塔尔萨的一家校车制造厂。

sentences.en: And this is a place that makes most of the yellow school buses we see in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是一个生产我们在美国看到的大多数黄色校车的地方，

sentences.en: where the workers were consistently working at over 90 degrees and they decided to go ahead and install a hundred million dollar cooling system.
sentences.zh: 那里的工人们经常在90度以上的环境中工作，他们决定继续前进并安装了一套价值一亿美元的冷却系统。

sentences.en: But that's that's a really hard check to write, I think, for a lot of companies, especially if you're not sort of a gigantic national company.
sentences.zh: 但对于许多公司来说，这绝对是一张很难开出的支票，特别是如果你不是那种巨型跨国公司的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like if you're a tiny mom and pop business, the expense might just be too much to bear.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你是一个微型的夫妻老婆店，这笔开销可能根本无法承受。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so I think this is genuinely a set of costs that employers have to look at, are looking at across the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这确实是全国各地的雇主不得不审视、也正在审视的一系列成本。

sentences.en: They're saying, you know, on one side, we're losing worker productivity.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你知道，一方面，我们正在失去工人的生产力。

sentences.en: We're losing worker hours.
sentences.zh: 我们正在失去工时。

sentences.en: I'm paying more workers comp.
sentences.zh: 我正在支付更多的工伤赔偿。

sentences.en: We're having to close on super hot days.
sentences.zh: 我们在超级热的日子里不得不关闭工厂。

sentences.en: All of that is like a really clear loss on one side of the ledger.
sentences.zh: 所有这些在账目的一边都是非常明确的损失。

sentences.en: On the other side is, well, you know, do I invest a hundred million dollars on indoor cooling or do I just take the hit in productivity?
sentences.zh: 另一边则是，你懂的，我是该花一亿美元投资室内降温，还是直接承受生产力损失？

sentences.en: But can employers just do that, like ignore what heat is doing to their workers?
sentences.zh: 但雇主真能这么做吗，比如无视高温对工人的影响？

sentences.en: Like, aren't there rules about that?
sentences.zh: 比如说，难道没有相关的规章制度吗？

sentences.en: In most of the country, there are no rules about that.
sentences.zh: 在全国大部分地区，对此都没有任何规章制度。

sentences.en: Again, speaking to the point that this is really a new experience for workers, for employers, for the economy, this level of exposure to heat.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，对于工人们、雇主们以及整个经济体来说，这种程度的高温暴露确实是一次全新的体验。

sentences.en: So right now, you know, OSHA, which is the federal agency that regulates workplace safety and has many,
sentences.zh: 所以现在，你知道的，OSHA，也就是负责监管职场安全的联邦机构，它有很多、

sentences.en: many rules in place for time limits on work and for safety and for exposure to all kinds of hazardous conditions.
sentences.zh: 很多关于工作时间限制、安全以及各类危险环境暴露的既定规则。

sentences.en: OSHA right now, there's no federal regulation that protects workers from exposure to heat or compels employers to protect their workers from heat exposure.
sentences.zh: 但目前OSHA还没有任何联邦法规来保护工人免受高温暴露，或者强制雇主保护工人免受高温伤害。

sentences.en: There are seven states currently that have some kind of state level regulation, but nothing in place at the national level.
sentences.zh: 目前有七个州制定了某种州级法规，但在国家层面上却是一片空白。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Are authorities trying to make some?
sentences.zh: 那当局有在试图制定一些吗？

sentences.en: I mean, given our new heat reality?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，鉴于我们面临的全新高温现实？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the Biden administration has directed OSHA to begin the process of crafting new federal regulations on heat and worker exposure.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府已经指示OSHA开始着手制定关于高温和工人暴露的全新联邦法规。

sentences.en: This is very new, this process.
sentences.zh: 这个过程非常新。

sentences.en: It could take as long as 10 years.
sentences.zh: 它可能需要长达10年的时间。

sentences.en: That's another thing I was surprised to learn when I did this reporting is just how long it can actually take to write national workplace safety regulations.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在做这篇报道时感到惊讶的一点，那就是编写国家职场安全法规实际上竟然需要这么长时间。

sentences.en: The expectation is, you know, what OSHA is working on is expected to set some kind of heat standards.
sentences.zh: 大家的期望是，你知道的，OSHA正在筹备的内容有望设定某种高温标准。

sentences.en: You know, workers who are working over a certain temperature or exposed to certain temperatures for a certain amount of time must be given breaks, must be given water.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在高于特定温度的环境下工作，或者在特定温度下暴露达到一定时长的工人，必须获得休息时间，必须获得饮用水。

sentences.en: Or indoor workplaces where workers are exposed to heat may need to install air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 或者对于工人会暴露在高温下的室内工作场所，可能需要安装空调。

sentences.en: That's sort of the expected standard that we're likely to see from this.
sentences.zh: 这差不多是我们从这当中有望看到的预期标准。

sentences.en: But that could be years away.
sentences.zh: 但这可能还要数年时间。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, there are a lot of business groups that are coming out and saying, hey, we don't want to see this.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，有许多商业团体站出来表示，嘿，我们不希望看到这个。

sentences.en: This could be too expensive.
sentences.zh: 这可能会太昂贵了。

sentences.en: We can figure this out ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们自己能解决好这事。

sentences.en: This is burdensome government regulation.
sentences.zh: 这是沉重的政府监管。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But, I mean, given our new heat reality, presumably something has to change.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，鉴于我们面临的全新高温现实，想必必须有所改变。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's changing already, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，改变已经在发生了，对吧？

sentences.en: Workers are already suffering.
sentences.zh: 工人们已经在遭受苦难了。

sentences.en: We're already taking the economic hit.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在承受经济上的打击了。

sentences.en: Someone who I interviewed in reporting this story was a former senior official at OSHA who said, this is going to cost a lot no matter what.
sentences.zh: 我在报道这个故事时采访的一位人士是OSHA的前高级官员，他表示，无论如何这都将付出巨大的代价。

sentences.en: Either employers are going to have to incorporate these new costs, you know, installing, cooling, giving a lot more breaks,
sentences.zh: 要么雇主必须将这些新成本纳入考量，你知道的，安装降温设施、提供更多的休息时间，

sentences.en: all the other costs that they will have to pay to protect their workers in the new world of heat.
sentences.zh: 以及他们为了在这个新的高温世界中保护工人而必须支付的所有其他成本。

sentences.en: And it's going to cost them a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且这会让他们付出沉重的代价。

sentences.en: And if they don't pay it, then we're going to see workers die.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不肯支付，那我们就会看到工人死亡。

sentences.zh: 科罗尔，谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你一起聊聊，萨布里娜。

sentences.en: There is no end in sight to a dangerous heat wave around 100 million Americans under excessive heat alerts this morning.
sentences.zh: 这场危险的热浪看不到尽头，今天早晨大约有1亿美国人处于极端高温预警之下。

sentences.en: In El Paso, Texas, temperatures have hit 100 for 43 straight days, while Phoenix, Arizona has seen a scorching 110 degrees for nearly 30 days in a row.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州埃尔帕索，气温已经连续43天达到100华氏度，而亚利桑那州菲尼克斯的酷热气温更是连续近30天达到110华氏度。

sentences.en: Heat may have led to the death of a local man in Death Valley.

sentences.en: The 71-year-old from Los Angeles collapsed outside a restroom yesterday when the temperature was 121 degrees.
sentences.zh: 这名来自洛杉矶的71岁老人昨天在气温高达121华氏度时晕倒在洗手间外。

sentences.en: And we've learned a letter carrier died Tuesday while walking his route in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 我们还了解到，一名邮政投递员周二在达拉斯步行送信时死亡。

sentences.en: Texas inmates are dying in sweltering prisons.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州的囚犯们正在酷热难耐的监狱里死去。

sentences.en: At least nine inmates have died since the relentless heat wave has gripped Texas.
sentences.zh: 自这股挥之不去的热浪席卷德州以来，至少已有九名囚犯死亡。

sentences.zh: 马里科帕县公布的最新数据显示，今年到目前为止，已有25人死于我们这挥之不去的高温。

sentences.en: Now tracking 39 heat-related deaths this summer, with more than 300 cases still waiting on confirmation.

sentences.en: Dana, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 达娜，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So Dana, we just heard from our colleague Coral Davenport about the economic effects of heat.
sentences.zh: 那么达娜，我们刚刚听了同事科罗尔·达文波特关于高温对经济影响的介绍。

sentences.en: And of course that has everything to do with how heat affects people and their bodies.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与高温如何影响人类及其身体息息相关。

sentences.en: And I think everybody has a kind of basic understanding that heat can be bad.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人对高温不好都有一个基本的理解。

sentences.en: But I don't think people really understand how, like the science of it.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得人们并不真正理解具体如何不好，也就是其中的科学原理。

sentences.en: Like what actually happens to our bodies in extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 比如极端高温究竟会对我们的身体造成什么影响。

sentences.en: So tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 所以请跟我讲讲这个吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a lot of people think of heat as an annoyance.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想很多人把高温只当成是一种烦恼。

sentences.en: I grew up in North Carolina, where it is famously hot and humid in the summers.
sentences.zh: 我在北卡罗来纳州长大，那里的夏天以炎热潮湿闻名。

sentences.en: And it's kind of a pain, but you don't think that it's deadly.
sentences.zh: 这确实挺让人头疼的，但你不会觉得它是致命的。

sentences.en: But I think what is a real surprise for people is that heat is actually the number one cause of death when it comes to extreme weather events.
sentences.zh: 不过我认为真正让人们感到意外的是，在极端天气事件中，高温其实是头号杀手。

sentences.en: So it really is a very serious thing that we have to account for, especially now with a warming planet.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一件非常严重的事情，我们必须高度重视，尤其是现在地球正在变暖。

sentences.en: The number one cause of weather-related death, like more than hurricanes or floods?
sentences.zh: 天气相关死亡的头号杀手，比飓风或洪水还多吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: It is the number one cause of death due to weather-related events is heat.
sentences.zh: 天气相关事件导致的头号死因就是高温。

sentences.en: Well, that's kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太惊人了。

sentences.en: So let's unpack it.
sentences.zh: 那我们来剖析一下吧。

sentences.en: What actually happens to people's bodies when they're exposed to extreme heat?
sentences.zh: 当人们暴露在极端高温下时，身体究竟会发生什么？

sentences.en: So the body has two main ways to cool itself down.
sentences.zh: 身体主要通过两种方式来为自己降温。

sentences.en: I think the first one we're all familiar with, which is sweat.
sentences.zh: 我想第一种大家都很熟悉，那就是出汗。

sentences.en: So our sweat glands on our skin start to produce sweat.
sentences.zh: 我们皮肤上的汗腺开始产生汗液。

sentences.en: And the goal is that that sweat evaporates off the body.
sentences.zh: 其目的是让这些汗液从身体表面蒸发掉。

sentences.en: And when it does, it cools the area underneath.
sentences.zh: 当汗液蒸发时，就会冷却下方的区域。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's, you're right, pretty known.
sentences.zh: 你说的对，这挺广为人知的。

sentences.en: So what's the other one?
sentences.zh: 那另一种方式是什么？

sentences.en: So the really cool part is the second aspect of the body's cooling mechanism, which is that it starts to increase blood flow.
sentences.zh: 非常酷的一点是身体降温机制的第二个方面，那就是它开始增加血流量。

sentences.en: So when it does that, the body is pushing more blood that normally circulates around your internal organs.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，身体会将原本在内脏器官周围循环的更多血液推动向体表。

sentences.en: And now it's redirecting that blood out to the surface of the skin.
sentences.zh: 现在它正将这些血液重新导向皮肤表面。

sentences.en: And that helps partly because the body can actually dissipate heat out through the skin.
sentences.zh: 这之所以有帮助，部分是因为身体实际上可以通过皮肤散发热量。

sentences.en: So it just releases heat into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是把热量释放到大气中。

sentences.en: But the really crazy part is that when the sweat evaporates off your skin and cools the area underneath, it's actually also cooling that blood that is now closer to the surface.
sentences.zh: 但真正疯狂的是，当汗液从你皮肤表面蒸发并冷却下方区域时，它实际上也在冷却现在更靠近表面的那些血液。

sentences.en: And that cooler blood can recirculate back to your internal organs and cool them down.
sentences.zh: 这些冷却后的血液可以重新循环回你的内脏器官，为它们降温。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So organs get hot.
sentences.zh: 所以器官变热了。

sentences.en: Blood takes the heat away from those organs to the surface of your skin.
sentences.zh: 血液将热量从这些器官带到你的皮肤表面。

sentences.en: It has contact with the air, which is cooler, and cools you down.
sentences.zh: 它与较凉爽的空气接触，从而为你降温。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So there's a really cool kind of two-step process with that sweat evaporation, then cooling the blood underneath the skin,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常酷的两步过程，通过汗液蒸发，然后冷却皮下血液，

sentences.en: and then hopefully cooling down the internal organs as it recirculates back through the body.
sentences.zh: 接着当血液在体内重新循环时，有望为内脏器官降温。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So enter extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 那么极端高温登场了。

sentences.en: So what happens when it gets hotter outside?
sentences.zh: 所以当外面变得更热时会发生什么？

sentences.en: So these two processes work really well in most conditions, but they do start to fail when it gets too hot or too humid.
sentences.zh: 在大多数条件下，这两种过程运作得非常好，但当气温过高或湿度过大时，它们就会开始失效。

sentences.en: So you have to think of your body and the environment kind of on a gradient in terms of temperature and moisture.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须从温度和湿度梯度的角度来考虑你的身体和周围环境。

sentences.en: So when your skin temperature, which is normally about 95 degrees Fahrenheit, is hotter than the air outside, your skin can actually release heat out into the environment.
sentences.zh: 所以当你的皮肤温度（通常约为95华氏度）高于室外空气时，你的皮肤实际上可以向环境中释放热量。

sentences.en: But when the air temperature is hotter than your skin, your skin starts to gain heat from the environment,
sentences.zh: 但当气温高于你的皮肤温度时，你的皮肤开始从环境中吸收热量，

sentences.en: and you can no longer cool down that way through the increased blood flow.
sentences.zh: 并且你无法再通过增加血流量这种方式来降温了。

sentences.en: The same happens with humidity.
sentences.zh: 湿度也是如此。

sentences.en: If it's too humid outside, if there's too much moisture in the air, the water on your skin, the sweat on your skin can't evaporate.
sentences.zh: 如果外面太潮湿，如果空气中的水分太多，你皮肤上的水分、你皮肤上的汗水就无法蒸发。

sentences.en: And so it just sits there or pulls off.
sentences.zh: 于是它只能停留在那里或者汇聚流淌。

sentences.en: So again, that cooling mechanism is loSt.
sentences.zh: 所以同样的，这种降温机制就失效了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So it's all about this gradient, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上一切都取决于这个梯度。

sentences.en: All of these processes in your body are interacting with the atmosphere around your body, what's going on in the air.
sentences.zh: 你体内的所有这些过程都在与你身体周围的大气、空气中的情况进行交互。

sentences.en: And if it's too humid, can't sweat.
sentences.zh: 如果湿度太大，就无法出汗。

sentences.en: If it's too hot, your body's going to take in heat as opposed to give it off.
sentences.zh: 如果温度太高，你的身体反而会吸收热量，而不是散发热量。

sentences.en: So that's a problem for the body.
sentences.zh: 这对身体来说是个问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So what exactly happens, like, inside your body when it gets too hot and humid?
sentences.zh: 那么当天气变得又热又湿时，你的身体内部究竟会发生什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So because of that increased circulation, the heart is really the most important organ when it comes to cooling down your body.
sentences.zh: 由于血液循环的增加，在为身体降温方面，心脏其实是最重要的器官。

sentences.en: So the heart is having to pump harder and faster.
sentences.zh: 所以心脏必须更用力、更快地跳动。

sentences.en: So your heart rate increases because it's trying to push blood further out, so out to the very surface of your skin.
sentences.zh: 你的心率会增加，因为它试图将血液输送到更远的地方，也就是输送到你皮肤的最表层。

sentences.en: So it's working a lot harder.
sentences.zh: 所以它工作得更加辛苦。

sentences.en: But at the same time, blood pressure can start to drop because there's not really an increased amount of blood volume.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，血压可能会开始下降，因为血液总量并没有实质性增加。

sentences.en: You're just pushing the same amount of blood to a wider surface area.
sentences.zh: 你只是在将等量的血液输送到更广阔的表面积。

sentences.en: So the heart is working harder, but your blood pressure is dropping.
sentences.zh: 所以心脏在更辛苦地工作，但你的血压却在下降。

sentences.en: Because that blood is trying to get all over the body instead of just in one area around the organs.
sentences.zh: 因为那些血液正试图流遍全身，而不仅仅是在器官周围的某个区域。

sentences.en: Therefore, the pressure is weaker and weaker the further out it gets.
sentences.zh: 因此，血液流得越远，压力就越弱。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And a drop in blood pressure is actually one of the most common causes of injury because someone might stand up if they've been sitting
sentences.zh: 血压下降其实是最常见的受伤原因之一，因为如果有人一直坐着然后站起来，

sentences.en: and they don't have enough blood going up to their head and then they can feel dizzy or faint.
sentences.zh: 而流向大脑的血液不足，他们就会感到头晕或昏厥。

sentences.en: So these are often really early signs that someone is really struggling from the heat is low blood pressure, dizziness, and potentially even fainting.
sentences.zh: 所以这些往往是某人正遭受高温严重折磨的极早期迹象，比如低血压、头晕，甚至可能昏厥。

sentences.en: Okay, so your body's working extra hard to increase your circulation and this is taxing your heart.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你的身体正在加倍努力以增加血液循环，这给你的心脏造成了沉重负担。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And in older people or people who have a pre-existing condition, especially one related to the heart, this can actually turn fatal.
sentences.zh: 对于老年人或患有基础疾病的人，尤其是与心脏相关的疾病，这实际上可能变成致命的。

sentences.en: This is how heat can kill them in the end, is by really taxing their heart.
sentences.zh: 这就是高温最终夺去他们生命的方式，也就是给心脏造成了过大的负担。

sentences.en: But in young, healthy people, this isn't as much of a problem.
sentences.zh: 但在年轻、健康的人身上，这倒不是什么大问题。

sentences.en: The heart is pretty resilient.
sentences.zh: 心脏相当有韧性。

sentences.en: The body is pretty resilient.
sentences.zh: 人体的适应能力其实很强。

sentences.en: And eventually, the increase in core temperature will plateau.
sentences.zh: 最终，核心体温的上升会进入一个平台期。

sentences.en: But if the temperatures are really extreme, 100 degrees or more, if someone is working out or working in the heat, then problems can start to arise.
sentences.zh: 但如果气温真的极高，达到100华氏度（约37.8摄氏度）甚至更高，或者有人在高温下运动或工作，问题就开始出现了。

sentences.en: You know, you can still continue to heat up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，体温仍然会继续上升。

sentences.en: So heat exhaustion or heat stress is one of the first really serious problems that can arise.
sentences.zh: 因此，中暑衰竭或热应激是最先出现的真正严重的问题之一。

sentences.en: And scientists think that's generally when the internal temperature of the body reaches about 100 to 103 degrees.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，这通常发生在人体内部温度达到大约100到103华氏度的时候。

sentences.en: And what exactly is heat exhaustion, Dana?
sentences.zh: 达娜，那究竟什么是中暑衰竭？

sentences.en: I hear it a lot and feel like myself, I have experienced it.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到这个词，感觉自己好像也经历过。

sentences.en: But what's going on scientifically in the body?
sentences.zh: 但在科学层面上，身体里究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's a real general sense of fatigue.
sentences.zh: 是的，它会带来一种非常普遍的疲惫感。

sentences.en: Also, your muscles might start not to function very well.
sentences.zh: 此外，你的肌肉可能开始无法正常运作。

sentences.en: And scientists think that this is actually a protective signal from the brain.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，这其实是大脑发出的保护性信号。

sentences.en: So your brain is actually telling your body to stop working, to sit down, to get somewhere shaded and cool, so it can try to cool itself off.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的大脑实际上是在命令你的身体停止工作，坐下来，找一个有阴凉且凉爽的地方，好让它设法自我降温。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So it makes you tired so that you do that.
sentences.zh: 所以它让你感到疲倦，好让你去这样做。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That is a really protective mechanism to try to prevent the next stage in the process, which is heat stroke, which can be deadly.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一种保护机制，试图阻止下一个阶段的到来，也就是可能致命的热射病。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me about heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 好的，那跟我讲讲热射病吧。

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So normally the body is really good at trying to prevent your body from heating up too faSt.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，身体非常擅长防止体温过快上升。

sentences.en: But if those mechanisms start to fail, so say that you're in really extreme conditions, maybe you're a worker and you have on heavy work equipment
sentences.zh: 但如果这些机制开始失效，比如你处于极端环境中，可能你是一名工人，穿着厚重的工作装备，

sentences.en: so that your sweat can't evaporate out into the environment, or if you're working hard or exercising and you're generating internal heat as well as gaining it from the outside,
sentences.zh: 导致你的汗水无法蒸发到环境中，或者如果你在高强度工作或运动，在从外界吸收热量的同时自己也在产生内热，

sentences.en: then your internal temperature can continue to rise even past the point of heat exhaustion, and that's when things get really dangerous.
sentences.zh: 那么你的内部体温就会超过中暑衰竭的点继续上升，而这正是情况变得极其危险的时候。

sentences.en: And what happens then?
sentences.zh: 那接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: So scientists think about 104 degrees is generally the cutoff for heat stroke, and at that point, you can start to have multi-organ failure.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，大约104华氏度通常是热射病的临界点，到了那个时候，你可能会开始出现多器官衰竭。

sentences.en: Okay, multi-organ failure.
sentences.zh: 好的，多器官衰竭。

sentences.en: So which organs are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 那我们具体指的是哪些器官？

sentences.en: So the organs that are most immediately and dangerously affected are the heart, which we've talked about a little bit, and then also the kidneys, the gut, and the brain.
sentences.zh: 受影响最直接、最危险的器官是心脏——我们刚才已经稍微聊过了，然后还有肾脏、肠道和大脑。

sentences.en: Okay, so heart, kidneys, gut, brain.
sentences.zh: 好的，也就是心脏、肾脏、肠道、大脑。

sentences.en: So start with the heart.
sentences.zh: 那就从心脏开始吧。

sentences.en: So I talked about this a little bit, but the heart is pumping harder and harder and harder.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚稍微提过，这时心脏在拼命、拼命、拼命地泵血。

sentences.en: So your heart rate is increasing, your blood pressure is dropping, and what happens when your blood pressure drops is that blood can't circulate to everywhere that it needs to go.
sentences.zh: 所以你的心率在加快，血压在下降，而血压下降带来的后果就是血液无法循环到需要它去的各个地方。

sentences.en: And so your organs slowly start to become deprived of oxygen, and that includes your heart.
sentences.zh: 因此，你的器官开始慢慢开始缺氧，这其中就包括你的心脏。

sentences.en: So it can even look like a heart attack where your heart was actually starved of oxygen because it just wasn't able to pump enough blood to the organs, including to itself.
sentences.zh: 所以它甚至看起来像是一次心脏病发作，因为你的心脏实际上处于缺氧状态，原因正是它无法为包括自身在内的各个器官泵送足够的血液。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the heart.
sentences.zh: 好的，心脏的情况就是这样。

sentences.en: What about the kidneys?
sentences.zh: 那肾脏呢？

sentences.en: The kidneys is really interesting because the brain actually sends a signal to the body that it should stop sending as much blood to the kidneys as it starts to get dehydrated.
sentences.zh: 肾脏的情况非常有趣，因为随着身体开始脱水，大脑实际上会向身体发送信号，要求减少输送到肾脏的血量。

sentences.en: So a quick refresher, you know, your kidneys are what are cleaning your blood, and then the waste gets excreted as urine.
sentences.zh: 简单复习一下，你的肾脏负责清洁血液，然后废物会作为尿液排出体外。

sentences.en: But that means that you're going to be losing a little bit of liquid.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着你会损失一些水分。

sentences.en: So if you're dehydrated, your body wants to preserve as much liquid as it possibly can, and so blood stops being pushed as much to the kidneys so that you don't lose any as urine.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你脱水了，你的身体会想要尽可能多地保留水分，因此就会减少向肾脏输送的血液，这样你就不会通过尿液损失水分了。

sentences.en: But as a result, your kidneys are then also starved of oxygen, and those cells can start to suffer and die.
sentences.zh: 但结果就是，你的肾脏也开始缺氧，那些细胞会开始受损并死亡。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So body is just trying to preserve liquid any way it can, but the effect of that is that oxygen stops flowing to the kidneys.
sentences.zh: 所以身体只是在想方设法保留水分，但这样做的后果就是氧气停止流向肾脏。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And your kidneys can survive for a little bit of time with reduced blood flow and reduced oxygen, but if that gets prolonged, you can start to have kidney failure.
sentences.zh: 在血流量和氧气减少的情况下，你的肾脏还能坚持一小段时间，但如果这种情况持续下去，你就会开始出现肾衰竭。

sentences.en: Okay, and you said also, Dana, the gut.
sentences.zh: 好的，达娜，你刚才还提到了肠道。

sentences.en: So how is my gut affected?
sentences.zh: 那我的肠道是怎么受影响的？

sentences.en: The gut is another area that blood is diverted from pretty quickly, and as a result, also has less oxygen going there.
sentences.zh: 肠道是另一个血液被相当快地抽离的部位，因此流向那里的氧气也会减少。

sentences.en: And when that happens, the gut can start to fail and break down a little bit, and you can start to have what we know as leaky gut.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，肠道功能可能会开始衰竭并出现一定程度的崩溃，你就会开始出现我们所说的肠漏症。

sentences.en: So the bacteria that's in your gut can actually start to travel out into the bloodstream, causing inflammation, and in really extreme and long-term situations, sepsis.
sentences.zh: 所以你肠道里的细菌实际上会开始游离进入血液，引起炎症，在极端的长期情况下，还会导致败血症。

sentences.en: Sepsis from heat?
sentences.zh: 因为中暑引起败血症？

sentences.en: That's kind of crazy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点疯狂。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: One of the emergency room physicians I spoke with said that sepsis is not a common cause of death when it comes to heat, normally because your other organs fail faster, frankly,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的一位急诊室医生说，说到中暑，败血症并不是常见的死因，坦白讲，通常是因为你的其他器官衰竭得更快，

sentences.en: but it is something that can occur.
sentences.zh: 但它的确是可能发生的情况。

sentences.en: Okay, so your heart is working over time, kidneys aren't getting enough oxygen, gut is leaking, so full-on multi-organ failure, as you're saying.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以你的心脏在超负荷运转，肾脏得不到充足的氧气，肠道在渗漏，正如你所说，也就是全面的多器官衰竭。

sentences.en: Yes, and not only the heart, the kidneys, and the gut, but also your brain.
sentences.zh: 是的，不仅是心脏、肾脏和肠道，还有你的大脑。

sentences.en: And when the brain is affected, things are getting really bad.
sentences.zh: 而当大脑受到影响时，情况就真的变得非常糟糕了。

sentences.en: So heat stroke, by definition, means that the brain is being affected.
sentences.zh: 因此，按定义来说，热射病意味着大脑已经受到了影响。

sentences.en: You know, you think stroke, you think brain.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一提到中风（stroke），就会想到大脑（brain）。

sentences.en: And so the reduced blood flow, the lack of oxygen, the increased temperature are affecting your brain just like every other organ.
sentences.zh: 所以血流量的减少、缺氧、体温的升高，正在像影响其他所有器官一样影响着你的大脑。

sentences.en: So what is really kind of perverse about heat stroke is that the body's internal thermometer is located in a part of the brain called the hypothalamus.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于热射病真正有些反常的地方在于，人体的内部温度调节中枢位于大脑中一个叫下丘脑的区域。

sentences.en: And if that starts to dysfunction or malfunction, then your body can actually stop cooling itself down.
sentences.zh: 如果这个部位开始功能失常或发生故障，那么你的身体实际上就会停止自我降温。

sentences.en: So oftentimes when people have really extreme heat stroke, they stop sweating.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，当人们患上极其严重的热射病时，他们会停止出汗。

sentences.en: Their skin might feel cool and clammy.
sentences.zh: 他们的皮肤可能会摸起来冰冷湿黏。

sentences.en: You know, they are no longer trying to cool their body down, even though their internal temperature is continuing to rise.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们不再试图为身体降温，尽管他们的内部体温仍在继续上升。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 唔。

sentences.en: So basically, kind of like the instinct to sweat and to have the body deal with this natural emergency state has gone.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，就像是出汗的本能以及身体应对这种自然紧急状态的机制消失了。

sentences.en: It's the brain is off kilter.
sentences.zh: 大脑失控了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It started to fail.
sentences.zh: 它开始罢工了。

sentences.en: So people also start to have dizziness, confusion, delirium.
sentences.zh: 所以人们还会开始出现头晕、意识模糊、神志不清的症状。

sentences.en: You're just no longer responding to your external environment, and that can really be deadly.
sentences.zh: 你 simplesmente 已经无法对外在环境做出反应，这真的可能是致命的。

sentences.en: So what's the fastest way to cool somebody off and save somebody if they get into this dangerous situation?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果有人陷入这种危险的境地，为某人降温并挽救生命的跑得最快的方法是什么？

sentences.en: It's an ice bath.
sentences.zh: 那就是冰水浴。

sentences.en: It sounds really simple, but it actually is the fastest way to cool down your internal temperature and try to prevent organ failure.
sentences.zh: 听起来很简单，但它确实是降低内部体温并试图防止器官衰竭的最快方法。

sentences.en: So this is even what they use in emergency rooms is kind of a glorified ice bath.
sentences.zh: 甚至连急诊室里用的也是这种经过改良升级的冰水浴。

sentences.en: And you can also do this in your home.
sentences.zh: 你在家里也可以这样做。

sentences.en: But is that not too drastic a temperature contrast?
sentences.zh: 但这难道不是太剧烈的温差对比了吗？

sentences.en: I asked an exercise physiologist about this because I thought the same, but he said that there's been a fair amount of research on this and there's a greater risk of heat
sentences.zh: 我曾就此询问过一位运动生理学家，因为我一开始也是这么想的，但他说这方面已经有过相当多的研究，与给身体带来某种温差休克的风险相比，

sentences.en: than there is of a kind of temperature change shock to your body.
sentences.zh: 热本身的风险要大得多。

sentences.en: So really, the most important thing you can do is to cool someone down as fast as possible and an ice bath is the way.
sentences.zh: 所以 realmente，你能做的最重要的事情就是尽快为某人降温，而冰水浴就是最佳途径。

sentences.en: Okay, so ice bath.
sentences.zh: 好的，冰水浴。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: I will remember that.
sentences.zh: 我会记住的。

sentences.en: Now, Dana, you mentioned earlier that people with heart conditions can be particularly susceptible to the dangers of extreme heat, which you just laid out
sentences.zh: 好了，达娜，你刚才提到有心脏病史的人特别容易受到极端高温的危害，而你刚刚已经用

sentences.en: in pretty frightening terMs.
sentences.zh: 相当吓人的词汇把这些危害剖析了一遍。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, are there other people or groups who are really vulnerable?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，还有其他人或群体是真正脆弱的吗？

sentences.en: I think this is really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: An earlier article I wrote during the summer heat waves looked at how elderly people are really uniquely vulnerable to heat.
sentences.zh: 我今年夏天在热浪期间写过的一篇文章探讨了老年人是如何对高温表现出独特脆弱性的。

sentences.en: And that's because both of our two cooling mechanisms, the sweating and the increased blood flow, are hampered in a lot of older adults.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们的两种降温机制——出汗和增加血流量——在许多老年人身上都受到了限制。

sentences.en: So older adults just don't sweat very much.
sentences.zh: 所以老年人往往不太出汗。

sentences.en: You know, their sweat glands produce less sweat than they used to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们的汗腺产生的汗水比以前少了。

sentences.en: And so that really important way to cool yourself down is just really not as available to you.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种对你而言至关重要的降温方式在他们身上确实大打折扣。

sentences.en: And then a lot of older adults, partly just because of age and partly because of pre-existing conditions, have decreased blood flow.
sentences.zh: 此外，许多老年人部分是因为年龄原因，部分是因为基础疾病，血流量有所减少。

sentences.en: So again, the heart is just not as able to push as much blood to the surface of the skin as happens in younger adults.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，心脏无法像在年轻人身上那样，将那么多的血液推送到皮肤表面。

sentences.en: Now, the good news is that older adults who are physically fit, they do still maintain these cooling mechanisms better than unfit older adults.
sentences.zh: 不过好消息是，身体健康的较老年人群确实比不健康的较老年人群更能维持这些降温机制。

sentences.en: So exercise is almost always the most important thing you can do for yourself health-wise, and it's the same when it comes to extreme heat.
sentences.zh: 因此，运动几乎永远是你为了健康能对自己做的最重要的事情，在面对极端高温时也是如此。

sentences.en: Dana, I think one of the things we're actually realizing is that this extreme heat is here to stay, right?
sentences.zh: 达娜，我觉得我们正在意识到的一点是，这种极端高温将会持续下去，对吧？

sentences.en: This is our new climate reality, and we'll have plenty more summers like this.
sentences.zh: 这是我们全新的气候现实，我们以后还会经历许许多多这样的夏天。

sentences.en: So in many ways, this is our new normal.
sentences.zh: 所以在许多方面，这就是我们的新常态。

sentences.en: So I guess I'm wondering, is there any way to adapt to this?
sentences.zh: 所以我想我在想，有什么办法可以适应这种情况吗？

sentences.en: There is some research that the human body can adapt to heat, and that is mostly in extreme athletes, so athletes who are doing, you know, long endurance training
sentences.zh: 确实有一些研究表明人体可以适应高温，这主要发生在极限运动员身上，也就是那些在高温环境下进行，

sentences.en: in high temperatures.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，长时间耐力训练的运动员。

sentences.en: And what scientists see is that they actually start these cooling mechanisms faster.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现，他们实际上会更早地启动这些降温机制。

sentences.en: So they start to sweat at lower temperatures, they have increased blood flow at lower temperatures, they also are more cardiovascularly fit, so their heart is just able
sentences.zh: 所以他们在较低的温度下就开始出汗，在较低的温度下血流量就会增加，他们的心血管健康状况也更好，所以他们的心脏能够

sentences.en: to withstand the stress of that increased blood flow and heart rate for longer.
sentences.zh: 承受血流量和心率增加带来的压力更长的时间。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: You know, I was a reporter in Baghdad in Iraq for a number of years, and it was a time when I was doing a lot of running,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我曾在伊拉克巴格达当过几年记者，那时候我经常跑步，

sentences.en: and we had this strip we would run on,
sentences.zh: 我们当时有一条常去跑步的路线，

sentences.en: and it was, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后你知道的，

sentences.en: 120 degrees at 8 p.m., and I remember doing that run and just feeling like, you know, my body was so taxed, but I got good at it, and then coming back to New York
sentences.zh: 晚上8点气温高达120华氏度（约48.9摄氏度），我记得当时去跑步，只觉得自己的身体负担太重了，但我后来适应了，然后回到纽约

sentences.en: and running in Central Park and thinking, oh my god, this is easy.
sentences.zh: 在中央公园跑步时心想，天哪，这太轻松了。

sentences.en: It was so much easier to run in a normal temperature than to run at 120, but I did get used to the 120.
sentences.zh: 在正常温度下跑步比在120华氏度的高温下跑步轻松太多了，但我确实习惯了120度的高温。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So the body is remarkable, and it actually can adapt to these extreme temperatures, but that is not realistic, frankly, for most people, especially, again, older adults
sentences.zh: 所以人体非常了不起，它确实能够适应这些极端温度，但坦白讲，这对于大多数人来说并不现实，尤其是，老年人

sentences.en: and people with preexisting conditions who are the most at risk for heat.
sentences.zh: 以及患有基础疾病、对高温风险最大的人群。

sentences.en: So while it is possible, it's really not the best strategy that we should just think that biologically we can adapt to these extreme temperatures.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然这种适应是可能的，但我们绝对不能仅仅指望在生物学上适应这些极端温度，这绝不是最佳策略。

sentences.en: I think we just really have to respect the heat and take it seriously, and I think that we're going to have to continue to adapt our behaviors and our lifestyles going forward
sentences.zh: 我认为我们真的必须对高温保持敬畏并认真对待它，而且我认为随着我们面对越来越高的温度，

sentences.en: as we deal with hotter and hotter temperatures.
sentences.zh: 我们在未来将不得不继续调整我们的行为和生活方式。

sentences.en: So that means air conditioning, cooling centers, dehydration, and doing those really practical behavioral ways to cool yourself down in these hot, hot climates.
sentences.zh: 这意味着空调、避暑中心、补水，以及在这些酷热气候中为自己降温的那些非常实用的行为方式。

sentences.en: So just being smart about heat is really essential and can be life-saving.
sentences.zh: 因此，在面对高温时保持理智至关重要，甚至能够挽救生命。
